items.t: Chinese Stock Markets Can't Quite Shake Off Bearish Sentiment
sum: Chinese stock markets remained on edge this week, with investor sentiment tilting bearish and tech shares remaining under pressure as the shock from the resignation of high-profile Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang reverberated through global markets.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.6 percent on Friday and 0.4 percent for the week. Its Nasdaq-style STAR Market 50 index tumbled 2.3 percent on Friday but managed a 1.8 percent gain for the week. The Shenzhen Component Index lost 1.9 percent for the week, and the tech-heavy ChiNext board retreated 1.3 percent after tanking 3.3 percent on Friday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 1.6 percent on Friday for a weekly loss of 3.5 percent. Its tech index dropped 3 percent.

The sharp decline in tech stocks was, in part, due to Huang's departure from the AI tech giant he co-founded and ran for three decades. He quit after revelations of an extramarital affair. In China's tech realm, Victory Giant Technology and TFC Communications dropped by the daily limit of 10 percent on Friday. Shares in optical transceiver giant Zhongji Innolight tumbled 8.4 percent, Eoptolink lost 8.8 percent, and electronics maker Foxconn retreated 7.5 percent.

"The exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia is due to have a huge impact, but at the moment, it's unclear how huge," said Dai Qing, an analyst with Changjiang Securities. "Suppliers and customers of Nvidia in China will have to wait for an evaluation, as well as will the rest of the world."

A Morgan Stanley gauge of Chinese mainland investor sentiment from November 5-11 fell 16 percentage points to 15 percent, with trading volumes contracting. The bank said it remains cautious on Chinese stocks, but favors shares traded on the Chinese mainland over those traded in Hong Kong.

Overall, Chinese equities have lost about US$3.5 trillion in value since May. To bolster the market, Beijing has taken steps to facilitate more equity investment by state-backed funds and more company share buybacks. The China Securities Regulatory Commission reiterated at an investor conference in Shanghai on Thursday that "there is long-term certainty in China's development, which lays a solid foundation for investment."

items.t: China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation (0386.HK) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation, an energy and chemical company, engages in the oil and gas and chemical operations in Mainland China. It operates through Exploration and Production, Refining, Marketing and Distribution, Chemicals, and Corporate and Others segments. The company explores and develops oil fields; produces and sells crude oil and natural gas; processes, purifies, imports, and trades in crude oil; manufactures, produces, sells, stores, and trades in petroleum products; owns and operates oil depots and service stations; and produces, markets, distributes, and sells refined petroleum products, including gasoline and diesel. It also manufactures, sells, markets, and distributes petrochemicals and derivative petrochemical products, and other chemical products, such as basic organic chemicals, synthetic resins, synthetic fiber monomers and polymers, synthetic fibers, synthetic rubber, and chemical fertilizers. In addition, the company explores, produces, and sells petroleum and natural gas; produces, stores, transports, and sells petrochemical and coal chemical products; produces and sells catalyst products, lubricant base oil, polyester chips and fibers, plastics, and petrochemical materials; and offers crude oil jetty and natural gas pipeline transmission services. Further, it engages in the production, sale, research, and development of ethylene and downstream byproducts; import and export of petroleum, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemical, other chemical products, and other commodities and technologies; research, development, and application of technologies and information; hydrogen energy business and related services, such as hydrogen production, storage, transportation, and sales; and battery charging and swapping, solar energy, wind energy, and other new energy business and related services. The company was incorporated in 2000 and is based in Beijing, China. China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation operates as a subsidiary of China Petrochemical Corporation.

items.t: SSE Composite Edges Up 0.10% to 3,689.91 as Shenzhen Outperforms and Oil Majors Slide
sum: Mainland Chinese stocks recovered from a weak open on Thursday 5 November 2026, with the Shanghai Composite eking out a small gain while the Shenzhen Component and ChiNext rallied on solar and computing-power names.

The Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index closed at 3,689.91 points on Thursday 5 November 2026, up 3.74 points, or 0.10 percent, from Wednesday's close of 3,686.17, according to Xinhua. The index opened at 3,646.57 and traded in a range between that level and an intraday high of 3,701.59, briefly reclaiming the 3,700 mark before easing in afternoon trade.

Thursday's modest gain extended a rebound that began on Wednesday, when the Shanghai Composite jumped 2.05 percent. That two-day recovery follows a sharp October sell-off that pushed the benchmark toward the bottom of its 52-week range of roughly 3,574 to 4,259. The index is still down about 3 percent over the past month and remains in negative territory for the year.

Growth-oriented boards outperformed. The Shenzhen Component Index rose 1.19 percent to 11,471.09, the ChiNext Index, China's Nasdaq-style board for growth companies, gained 0.87 percent to 2,566.80, and the STAR Composite Index, covering the Shanghai sci-tech innovation board, advanced 1.38 percent to 1,546.42.

Turnover across stocks covered by the Shanghai and Shenzhen benchmarks rose to about 2.12 trillion yuan, roughly $316 billion, from 2.04 trillion yuan on Wednesday. Rising volume on an up day is a constructive sign for market breadth, and more than 4,700 stocks across the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges were trading higher at the peak of the morning rebound.

The session started on a nervous note. The Shanghai Composite fell as much as 1.07 percent at the open and ChiNext dropped about 2 percent in early trade, as investors digested overnight volatility in US semiconductor stocks and the sharp fall in crude prices. Sentiment then shifted quickly from caution to broad-based buying, a pattern described by local media as a V-shaped rebound.

Support measures announced earlier in the week underpinned the recovery. Chinese authorities rolled out targeted liquidity injections, lowered interest rates on loans used to fund share buybacks and eased restrictions on leveraged trading.

Shenzhen Component closes 1.63% higher at 11,010.68
sum: The Shenzhen Component ended Monday's session at 11,010.68 points, up 1.63% from the previous close. The dated closing figure was reported by Xinhua. The index gained 176.90 points from its October 30 close of 10,833.78, according to Bloomberg.

The rebound followed a sharp sell-off in the previous session and came as reports pointed to possible additional measures to stabilize Chinese equities. Trading Economics reported that regulators were considering discussions with major banks on expanding lending support for stock buybacks. The same report said a major state-owned bank planned to extend up to 200 billion yuan in additional loans to two state asset-management firms. These reports describe policy expectations rather than a confirmed completed intervention.

Trading activity also increased. Xinhua said turnover for stocks covered by the Shanghai Composite and Shenzhen Component reached about 1.8 trillion yuan, compared with 1.69 trillion yuan on the previous trading day. Higher turnover alongside the index rebound suggests that participation broadened during the recovery, but it does not by itself establish whether the move will persist.

Sector performance was uneven. Xinhua identified AI comic drama and gaming shares among the market's leaders, while precious metals, banking, coal, and oil and gas stocks posted losses. Trading Economics listed PetroChina, Kweichow Moutai, CATL, and BYD among notable gainers, with their respective advances ranging from 1.30% to 3.38%.

The broader backdrop remained mixed. Trading Economics reported that China's official manufacturing PMI declined to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, while the non-manufacturing PMI fell to 49.7 from 50.2. The data point to continuing economic pressure even as policy expectations supported Monday's risk appetite. For investors, the session therefore combined a strong technical rebound from a more than one-year low with unresolved questions about domestic demand and the durability of official support.

sum: Asia split on Monday. Oil and bank shares lifted Hong Kong and Shanghai, India’s benchmark staged an afternoon recovery, and Tokyo fell for a third session as chip stocks extended their slide ahead of four central bank decisions this week.
The BSE SENSEX rose 0.66% to 73,606.75, the Hang Seng Index gained 0.51% to 23,211.81, the SSE Composite edged up 0.19% to 3,697.52 and the Nikkei 225 fell 0.80% to 62,189.65.

The common thread was a rotation out of technology and AI hardware stocks, which had been hit by a weak Friday session on Wall Street, and into energy, banks and defensive sectors. Asian markets closed before Anthropic’s IPO filing lifted US technology shares later on Monday. Each section below covers the closing level, the drivers, the leading and lagging stocks and what to watch next.

Elsewhere in the region, South Korea’s Kospi fell 1.46% to 5,469.47, slipping below the 5,500 mark as Samsung Electronics declined, while energy producers outperformed across Asian markets. Oil prices stayed elevated during Asian hours before easing later in the global session, and the dollar traded near 157 yen. Investors across the region are positioning for four central bank decisions this week: the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Canada on Wednesday, the European Central Bank on Thursday and the Bank of Japan on Friday.
Nikkei 225 Falls 0.80% to 62,189.65, Its Lowest Close Since July, as Chip Stocks Extend Their Slide
Tokyo’s price-weighted benchmark dropped for a third straight session as semiconductor shares sold off, even though more stocks rose than fell and the broader Topix finished higher.

The Nikkei 225 closed at 62,189.65 on Monday, 26 October 2026, down 503.51 points or 0.80% from Friday’s close of 62,693.16, according to index provider Nikkei Inc. It was the index’s third consecutive decline and its lowest close since 30 July.

Delegates from across the marine fuels industry are gathering in Singapore this week for the 24th Singapore International Bunkering Conference and Exhibition (SIBCON), the world's largest bunkering event.

Held every two years and organised by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), the conference and exhibition returns to Resorts World Sentosa from October 13-15 after a 2024 edition that drew more than 1,800 participants from over 60 countries.

This year's programme, with more than 80 speakers, is built around the theme "Charting a Resilient Multi-Fuel Future", taking in geopolitics, regulation, digitalisation and decarbonisation as they bear on a market now supplying several fuels at once.

sum: As the conflict in the Middle East weakens supply chains, China aims to increase its production of ethylene in its first fully green production chain.

PetroChina announced that its subsidiary Dushanzi Petrochemical began operating a new ethylene production line in the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region on Thursday. The expansion adds 1.2 million tons to the company’s annual production capacity, raising its total capacity in the region to 3 million tons.

The project is aimed at becoming the largest ethylene production hub in central and western China, according to South China Morning Post. Most of the industry has been positioned along the coast up until now, away from the key resources. The project will allow China to produce a key industrial chemical while supporting national energy security and carbon reduction goals.

The expansion would “reshape the long-standing east-west geographic imbalance of domestic ethylene capacity, while enhancing the resilience and security of energy and chemical supply chains,” South China Morning Post reports. And it would also demonstrate China’s commitment to reducing the industry’s environmental impact.
Known as “industrial gold” in China, ethylene is an important petroleum-based chemical used in many industrial products, including plastics, synthetic fibers, and advanced materials.
China is currently the world’s largest producer of ethylene, with annual production capacity exceeding 62 million tonnes by the end of last year, according to South China Morning Post.

However, 65% of China’s ethylene industry output has come from the eastern coast. The Xinjiang expansion is part of an effort to increase production in western areas that hold the most oil and gas resources.

Woodside Denies ExxonMobil Takeover Approach as Shares Slide 2.7%
sum: Woodside Energy said on Monday it was not aware of any proposal from ExxonMobil and was not engaged in discussions regarding a potential transaction. The Australian group responded to media speculation fuelled since Friday by a Bloomberg report indicating the US major was considering a takeover of Woodside to deepen its presence in liquefied natural gas (LNG) and Asian markets. "Woodside is not aware of any proposal and confirms it is not in discussions regarding a potential transaction with ExxonMobil Corporation," the company said in a statement issued Monday.

Woodside shares fell 2.7% at the open of the Australian stock exchange on Monday. Oil prices simultaneously dropped 4%, hitting their lowest level since March, after the United States and Iran announced an initial deal to end their conflict and reopen traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. ExxonMobil Australia declined to comment. Australian rival Santos fell a steeper 4.3% in early trade.

On Friday, Woodside's secondary US-listed shares had surged 8.35% following the Bloomberg report. According to those reports, ExxonMobil was seeking to deepen its LNG presence and secure direct access to Asian markets, notably Japan and South Korea. Acquiring Woodside would give the US major a portfolio of operational export infrastructure in Western Australia as well as long-term supply contracts.

Australia's leading LNG exporter, Woodside recently increased its stake in the Browse project to about 42% by pre-empting a sale by PetroChina of its 10.67% share to Inpex. The Browse project is described as Australia's largest undeveloped conventional gas resource. The move consolidates Woodside's operational control over one of its most strategic gas assets, for which a final investment decision has yet to be taken.

According to a sector analysis note, Woodside would have recorded a production high in 2025 of 198.8 million barrels of oil equivalent (MMboe), or around 545,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, with production costs at $7.8/boe.

sum: On March 29, PetroChina Company Limited (601857.SH, 00857.HK) released its 2025 annual report. The report shows that due to the decline in international oil prices, the company's annual revenue and net profit decreased year-on-year, but the profit scale remained high, cash flow performance was strong, and a high dividend plan was proposed.
Core Performance: Revenue and Net Profit Both Declined, Daily Profit of 430 Million Yuan

In 2025, PetroChina achieved operating revenue of 2.86 trillion yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 2.5%; net profit attributable to shareholders of the parent company was 157.302 billion yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 4.5%, with a daily profit of approximately 430 million yuan. Basic earnings per share were 0.86 yuan, a decrease of 0.04 yuan compared to the previous year. The company stated that the decline in revenue was mainly due to the combined impact of falling prices and changes in sales volume of oil and gas products such as crude oil and refined oil.
Industry Background: International Oil Prices Fell Year-on-Year, Multiple Adjustments in Domestic Refined Oil Prices

In 2025, the global crude oil market experienced loose supply and demand, coupled with geopolitical conflicts and changes in trade patterns, leading to a year-on-year decline in international oil prices. The annual average price of Brent crude oil futures was $68.19 per barrel, and the average price of U.S. WTI crude oil futures was $64.73 per barrel, both down 14.6% year-on-year. The company's average realized crude oil price was $64.11 per barrel, a year-on-year decrease of 14.2%.

Domestic refined oil prices were adjusted in sync with international oil prices, with the state making 19 adjustments throughout the year. The prices of standard gasoline and diesel products decreased by a cumulative 915 yuan/ton and 880 yuan/ton, respectively.
Business Segments: Upstream Profits Under Pressure, Natural Gas Segment Grew Against the Trend

items.t: PetroChina says operations 'overall normal', Strait of Hormuz accounts for about 10% of its supplies
PetroChina plots $32bn development drive, downplays Iran impact
China’s crude import stress resistance in a Hormuz crisis
sum: As the Gulf conflict escalates and the near-full closure of the Strait of Hormuz enters its second week, the likelihood of broader production disruptions in the Gulf and refinery run cuts across Asia is increasing.

In China, the world’s largest crude importer and potentially one of the most exposed economies in the event of a prolonged Middle East supply disruption, some refiners have already brought forward previously scheduled maintenance in anticipation of possible feedstock shortages.

While the country benefits from a diverse supplier base and sizable crude inventories, uneven stock distribution and varying dependence on Middle Eastern supplies leave some refineries facing more immediate run-cut risks. This report assesses these vulnerabilities at the refinery level.
Oil supply overview: national reserves likely only an emergency buffer
In 2025, crude supplied via the Strait of Hormuz accounted for roughly 35% of China’s total crude supplies, including both seaborne and non-seaborne sources.

China’s seaborne crude imports averaged about 11.5mbd in the first two months of the year, around 900kbd higher than the 2025 average. The increase was mainly driven by pre-holiday refinery run hikes, alongside roughly 200kbd of inventory builds.

At the same time, the share of seaborne imports transiting Hormuz declined from 51% in 2025 to about 44%. This reflects a sharp increase in Russian seaborne crude imports, which do not pass through the Strait, rising from around 1.2mbd in 2025 to roughly 1.8mbd. Private Chinese refiners stepped up purchases as weaker demand from other Asian buyers created opportunities, reducing reliance on Hormuz-linked Iranian supplies.

items.t: Are Shell, Mitsubishi trying to pull out of LNG Canada? Probably not, analysts say
sum: Speculation that Shell PLC and Mitsubishi Corp. are looking to exit LNG Canada is misplaced, analysts say, with some arguing the reported stake-sale talks could even signal preparations for expansion rather than a pullback.

The companies have so far declined to comment on the Reuters report from earlier this month that the partners were exploring sale options for their stakes in the major liquefied natural gas terminal in Kitimat, B.C.

Global oil and gas major Shell, which holds the largest stake in LNG Canada at 40 per cent, is looking to sell up to three-quarters of its holding, according to the report. Mitsubishi currently holds a 15 per cent stake in the project, with the remaining equity held by Petroliam Nasional Berhad (better known as Petronas), MidOcean Energy LLC, PetroChina Co. Ltd. and Korea Gas Corp.

items.t: Oil & Gas Companies in Singapore: Investable Stocks Guide
sum: For many Singapore investors, oil & gas companies in Singapore can feel like a black box. You hear about big refineries on Jurong Island and global trading houses setting up here, but you may only see a handful of energy-related counters on SGX. Most of the top petroleum companies operating here are either listed overseas or privately held, which makes it harder to see what you can realistically invest in.

This guide narrows that gap. Along the way, you’ll get a practical framework to analyse these businesses, understand their risks, and decide how (and whether) they should fit into a Singapore-focused investment portfolio.

Stay in control of your own decisions with an MAS-regulated, execution-only service and transparent pricing—so you can build and manage your energy exposure more easily across markets.

Singapore is one of the world’s top three oil trading and refining hubs, with the country’s three main refineries having a combined crude oil refining capacity of roughly 1.3–1.5 million barrels per day. These refineries sit within a broader ecosystem of storage terminals, LNG infrastructure and petrochemical complexes primarily clustered around Jurong Island.

However, most of the high-profile oil & gas companies in Singapore that run refineries or trading businesses—such as the local arms of ExxonMobil and others—are subsidiaries of foreign-listed parents rather than standalone listings on the Singapore Exchange.
In other words, Singapore is huge in the global oil trade, but the number of energy stocks you can actually buy on SGX is relatively small.
